name: Taha Mikati
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2020)
forbes_bio: Taha Mikati cofounded Beirut-based holding company M1 Group.
Its investments include stakes in South African telecom firm MTN, fashion retailer Pepe Jeans and prime real estate in New York, London and Monaco.
Mikati and his billionaire brother Najib founded Investcom in 1982, selling satellite phones at the height of Lebanon's civil war.
They expanded into Africa where they built cellphone towers in Ghana, Liberia and Benin, among other countries.
In 2005, Investcom went public on the London Stock Exchange, and in 2009, South Africa's MTN bought the Mikatis' stake for $3.6 billion.
forbes_facts: Mikati bought a bunch of satellite phones and sold them to friends and associates in Beirut in the early 80s for $50,000 apiece.
Mikati's son Azmi is the CEO of M1 Group.

name: Issad Rebrab
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Isaad Rebrab founded Cevital and served as its CEO for more than 50 years; He named his son, Malik, CEO in July 2022.
Cevital, Algeria's biggest privately-held company, owns one of the largest sugar refineries in the world, with the capacity to produce 2 million tons a year.
Cevital owns European companies, including French home appliances maker Groupe Brandt and Spanish aluminum firm Alas Iberia.
After serving 8 months in jail on charges of corruption, Rebrab was released on January 1, 2020. He denies any wrongdoing.
In May 2023, an Algerian court barred Rebrab from exercising any commercial or management duties at Cevital.
forbes_facts: Rebrab is the son of militants who fought for Algeria's independence from France.
Cevital helped finance a biopic on Algerian resistance hero Larbi Ben M'hidi, who was executed by the French in 1957.

name: Roberto Irineu Marinho
name_chinese: 罗伯托·伊里纽马林尼奥
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Roberto Irineu Marinho and his two billionaire brothers, Joao Roberto and Jose Roberto, inherited control of Globo, Brazil's largest media group.
Grandfather Irineu Marinho started Globo in 1925 with a newspaper. He died 25 days after the first issue was published and his son Roberto took over.
Globo Group includes Brazil's largest broadcaster, Rede Globo, Brazil's largest newspaper company and Globosat, Brazil's largest pay TV provider.
In December 2017, Roberto Irineu quit as the executive president of the group. For the first time ever, a non-family member assumed that position.
He remains vice-president of the board of directors, which is chaired by his brother Joao Roberto Marinho.
forbes_facts: The low profile media baron also owns Sertaozinho Farm, which produces Orfeu gourmet coffee.
In the 1970s, he worked as an intern at U.S. TV network ABC.

name: Su Suyu
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023-2025); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026); Hurun China (2008-2026)
forbes_bio: Su Suyu is the controlling shareholder of Shanghai-listed power generation company Luenmei Quantum.
Su, one of the world's richest self-made women, co-founded the predecessor company of the Luenmei Group with two sons in Shantou.
Su also has interests in real estate, minerals and finance. She shares her fortune with her sons.

name: Jennifer Pritzker
sec_insider_companies: ORTHOPEDIATRICS CORP (KIDS) - TenPercentOwner; Alphatec Holdings, Inc. (ATEC) - TenPercentOwner
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Jennifer Pritzker is one of 13 billionaire heirs in the Chicago-based Pritzker clan.
A retired Army lieutenant colonel, she came out as a transgender woman in 2013.
She inherited stakes in her family's Hyatt Hotels chain as well as industrial firms run by her late father Robert and his brothers Jay & Donald.
Pritzker is also the founder and CEO of private wealth management firm Tawani Enterprises.
In 2003, she opened the Pritzker Military Museum and Library in Chicago, which features a collection of more than 65,000 books and military artifacts.
forbes_facts: Pritzker responded to Donald Trump's proposed ban on transgender people in the military by offering to help find "a better solution."
Pritzker's Tawani Foundation donates to educational initiatives, military history preservation and LGBTQ organizations.

name: Anna Angelicoussis
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Anna Angelicoussis owns Greek shipping firms Alpha Bulkers, Alpha Gas and Pantheon Tankers Management.
Angelicoussis previously owned a number of other shipping firms with her brother John Angelicoussis (d. 2021) but split off to form her own business in 2000.
Together her firms own 83 oil tankers, liquefied natural gas carriers and bulk carriers.
Her niece Maria Angelicoussis inherited John's companies and is now Greece's richest person.

name: Nandan Nilekani
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2007-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun India (2015-2022); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Nandan Nilekani is the cofounder of tech giant Infosys and its non-executive chairman since 2017.
Nilekani, who left Infosys in 2009, was brought back in 2017 after a boardroom shakeup at the company and the sudden departure of its CEO.
Nilekani is credited with building Aadhaar, India's mammoth identity card scheme, during his tenure as chairman of the Unique Identification Authority of India.
The tech magnate, who still has shares in Infosys, has backed Fundamentum, a venture capital fund aimed at technology companies.
In 2023, he donated $38 million to the Indian Institute of Technology, Bombay, his alma mater, to expand research and infrastructure.
forbes_facts: He teamed up with Ratan Tata, former chairman of the Tata Group, to start Avanti Finance to provide microloans to the poor.
He and wife Rohini have signed the Giving Pledge. They run separate philanthropic arms, which focus on areas such as urbanization and biodiversity.

name: Wu Yiling
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2011-2026)
forbes_bio: Wu Yiling is the honorary chairman of Yiling Pharmaceutical, a supplier of cardiovascular and flu drugs, among others.
Wu, whose father was a doctor, practiced Chinese medicine for 11 years himself before he founded Yiling Pharmaceutical in 1992.
Yiling's Lianhua Qingwen capsules have been recommended by China health experts for treating mild Covid cases.
The company is listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange.

name: Nicola Bulgari
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2002-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Nicola Bulgari is vice chairman of luxury goods brand Bulgari, which was founded by his great-grandfather.
Bulgari established itself as a global luxury brand in jewelry, watches, fragrances, apparel, hotels and resorts.
In 2011, the Bulgari family sold its controlling stake to luxury goods conglomerate LVMH for $5.2 billion in cash and stock.
Nicola Bulgari is well known for his car collection, which includes mostly American cars from 1920s to the 1940s.
forbes_facts: He once turned down an offer from Andy Warhol to exchange a painting for Bulgari jewels. "It was the worst deal of my life," he said.
Bulgari built a 21-acre complex in Allentown, Pennsylvania with 7 warehouses and 4 restoration shops, home to roughly 125 cars.

Hu graduated from the Huazhong University of Science and Technology.
Fellow billionaire Gong Hongjia was an early Hikvision investor and is its current vice chairman.

name: Subhash Runwal
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2024); Forbes annual (2015-2023); Hurun Global (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Mumbai property tycoon Subhash Runwal chairs the Runwal Group, known for building middle class homes in the city's central suburbs.
It also owns several malls and counts the Singapore government's GIC as a key investor in that business.
A trained accountant, Runwal was born in a small town in Maharashtra and migrated to Mumbai at age 21.
He worked as an accountant for nearly a decade before taking the plunge into real estate in 1978.
forbes_facts: Runwal's lives in a sea-front home in Mumbai  next to Bollywood star Shah Rukh Khan.
Runwal's first job as an accountant got him a U.S. posting but he returned home in six months as he couldn't adjust to the lifestyle.
